opening.headline: The problem of uploading a large PDF and receiving an answer that appears to have been only partially read is solved by understanding the file format and volume limitations and dividing the data.
body: When I uploaded a 300-page PDF of the annual report, only the contents of the first chapter appeared in the answer, and when asked about the second half, which contains many tables, the answer was blank or general. Some files may be refused upload altogether. I know there is a limit, but it's hard to know what the limit is.

In this class, we will examine file limits divided into four axes: format, number, size, and content type. Compare ChatGPT, Gemini Notebook, and Claude's guidance, and learn how to segment and summarize large documents and complement tables and images with text. At the end, we will look at examples of dividing the annual report into chapters and the judgment order for determining which data will be subject to limitations.

screens.lead:
First, let's look at problems that arise when uploading large files. Pay attention to how the responses vary from question to question.

visual.alt: The response reflects only the 300-page PDF icon on the left and the first part on the right.

paragraphs: When I uploaded a 300-page PDF of the annual report, only the contents of the first chapter appeared in the answer. Questions in the latter part of the table, which have many votes, come back with blank or general answers. Some files may be refused upload altogether.
I know there are limits, but it's hard to know where they are and whether everything is read well within the limits.
The question for this class is this. How do you know the limits of file format and size, and how do you respond?

screens.outro: First, let me recall your experience.

screens.title: Have you ever had problems with files being too large?
screens.lead: When you select each question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. You will not enter or submit your answer, so think first before clicking.

items.prompt: Has your upload been blocked or only partially read?
items.answer: Blocked uploads are a clear sign that format, number, or size limits have been reached. On the other hand, if it seems that only part of it has been read, even if it is within the limit, there is a lot of content, so it may be that necessary pieces were not used, so the cause is less noticeable.

items.prompt: Have you ever uploaded a large document divided into chapters?
items.answer: If you have experience posting in parts, you will have a better chance of finding the pieces that fit your question. This is the basic idea of ​​partitioning that we will cover in this lesson. The unit of division is not pages, but chapters or topics.

items.prompt: Are there limits not only on size, but also on number of files, format, and type of content?
items.answer: There is. Limits arise from four axes: format, number of files, size, and content type, that is, the proportion of tables and images. It's easy to think that just matching the size will solve the problem, but you need to check all four axes.

screens.outro: Now that I've summarized my experience, let's first check what formats I can upload.

screens.title: File Formats: What You Can Upload
screens.lead: Select each tab to see the file formats received for each product. Note that there is a difference between what format is supported and what is readable.

visual.alt: Illustration showing a line of format icons and the scope of support for each product.
labels: Depending on the type, processing may be less smooth.

tabs.label: ChatGPT Project
tabs.body: You can upload PDFs, spreadsheets, documents, images, or paste text into your ChatGPT project. Uploaded files can be opened, previewed, downloaded, and deleted from the source list. If you upload a file with the same name, you can add it with Upload anyway or skip it with Skip. GPT supports most documents, spreadsheets, images, text, and code files, but the format it receives varies depending on the model, and some formats require the Code Interpreter & Data Analysis setting to be turned on.

tabs.label: Claude Project
tabs.body: The Claude project posts documents, text files, and code snippets to its knowledge base. The uploaded data will be used in all chats of the project. On paid plans, when your knowledge approaches the context limit, RAG mode is automatically turned on to increase capacity.

tabs.label: Gemini Notebook
tabs.body: Gemini Notebook has the widest range of source formats. Sources include PDF, docx, txt, md, csv, pptx, ePub files, audio such as MP3 and WAV, pasted text, web URLs, public YouTube videos, Google Docs, Slides, and Sheets. Images support avif, gif, heic, jpeg, png, webp, etc., but please note that processing may be less smooth depending on the type of image.

tabs.label: Common precautions
tabs.body: Saying that a format is supported means that you can upload it, but it doesn't mean that the content will be read accurately. Letters in scanned images, complexly placed tables, and figures in pictures may not be read as reliably as text. GPT instructions also recommend text-oriented files rather than complex layouts.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the format, let's compare the limits on number of files and size.

screens.title: Number of files and size limits: Compare product-specific guidance
screens.lead: The table below compares the guidance for each product. Read each row from left to right to see what units the limits are in.

data.caption: Information on the number of files and size limits for each product
rows: The number of files you can upload varies depending on your plan.
You can preview, download and delete files from the source list.
If you upload a file with the same name, select Upload anyway or Skip.
You can attach up to 20 files to one GPT.
One file can be up to 512MB.
Text-centered files are better to use than complex layouts.
Free users can add up to 50 sources.
One source can be up to 500,000 words or 200 MB uploaded file. Google Slides is limited to 100 tokens, and Google Sheets is limited to 100,000 tokens.
If there are more than five sources, they are categorized into topic labels.
Free users can create up to five projects.
On paid plans, when you get close to your limit, RAG mode increases your capacity by up to 10x.

data.notes: The numbers in the table are instructions written in the help of each product. It is important to note that the limits vary from product to product. One place provides guidance by the number of files, and the other provides information by the number of words or tokens, so the limit for the same data may vary depending on the product. Rather than memorizing numbers, remember which axis the limit is set on.

screens.outro: Now that we know what the limits look like, let's look at how to split and summarize large data.

screens.title: Segmentation and summarization, processing of tables and images
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to follow how the 300-page PDF is divided into multiple files. Pay attention to what each file does.

visual.alt: A schematic of a large document being split into chapter fragments, summary files, and table description files.

steps.title: Divide: by chapter or topic
steps.body: By dividing large documents into smaller files by chapter or topic, it becomes easier to find the pieces that fit your question. In a 300-page file, the pieces that match the financial questions are buried in numerous pages, but if you have a file that contains only the financial chapters, the questions and files correspond immediately. The file name is also given to reveal the contents.

steps.title: Summary: Full Contour File
steps.body: Keeping a summary file of all the essentials can help your assistant get an overview first. It serves as a guide to what content is in which chapter, helping you find which file your question relates to.

steps.title: Organization: Sort by label
steps.body: If there are more than five sources, Gemini Notebook automatically labels and classifies them by topic, and you can also change the label name or move the source to another label. The more files you have, the more you need to organize them.

steps.title: Tables and Images: Sentence Description File
steps.body: Tables and images are harder to read than text. Please note that processing may be less smooth depending on the type of image source. If possible, it is safer to place key figures in tables and images in separate auxiliary files, translated into sentences.

screens.outro: Now that you know the method, let's compare the effect of applying it to an actual annual report.

screens.title: Commentary: Effects of overall annual report and division into chapters
screens.lead: Switch between full and split uploads and compare how the answers and evidence for the same question change.

states.label: upload all
states.body: I uploaded the entire PDF file of the annual report and asked what the operating profit was in the third quarter. The responses were general, based on the preceding outline sentences. The financial figures were in the latter part with lots of tables, and there were hundreds of pages in one file, so I couldn't seem to find the piece that fit the question. The answers either did not have specific numbers or contained incorrect numbers. If you had just trusted the fact that the file was uploaded and used the response as is, incorrect numbers could have been included in the report. The fact that this problem occurred even though the file was within the limit shows that being within the limit does not guarantee that it will be read successfully.

states.label: split upload
states.body: The same report was divided into 01-Overview, 02-Market, 03-Business Division, and 04-Finance. When I asked the same question, 04-Finance was used as the basis and the value came out accurately. There were a few tricks. The content is revealed in the file name, and Chapter 04, which has many tables, includes an auxiliary file that translates key figures into sentences, and a two- or three-line summary is added at the beginning of each chapter file to make it easier to search. After dividing in this way, we checked whether the same value was obtained by asking the same question twice, and also checked whether 04-Financial File was cited in products with citations.

screens.outro: Now that we have confirmed the effect, we will organize the order in which data is subject to the limit.

screens.title: Explanation: Judgment order to determine which data will be subject to the limit
screens.lead: Click the Next Step button to proceed through the judgment sequence, which opens four questions one after another. As data passes through the flowchart, the processing method is determined.

steps.title: Question 1: Is the format supported?
steps.body: First, check that the format of the file you want to upload is the format accepted by the product. If the format is not supported, convert to PDF or text. Scanned images will be read more reliably if you convert them into a text file.

steps.title: Question 2: Is the number of files close to the limit?
steps.body: If the number of files is close to the limit, combine files with similar topics into one. Since the goal is to reduce the number, select files with overlapping content first. For example, combine multiple FAQ articles for the same product into one. However, we will check again in the next question whether the combined files will become too large.

steps.title: Question 3: Is one file close to the size or volume limit?
steps.body: If the size or volume of one file is close to the limit, split it into chapters. Even if the content is within the limit, necessary pieces may be buried, so it is safer to split it before the limit is reached.

steps.title: Question 4: Are there a large proportion of tables and images?
steps.body: Materials with lots of tables and images can be difficult to read. An explanation file containing key figures and contents translated into sentences is provided as an auxiliary file. The method is to leave the original as is and add a description file. In the description file, write down the table title, column names, and key row values ​​in sentences.

steps.title: Closing: Confirmation with representative questions
steps.body: After the judgment is made, we ask three representative questions to check whether it has been reflected. Representative questions are chosen to target different parts of the material, such as about the overview, about the figures in the tables, or about later chapters. If it is not reflected even after passing all four axes of format, number, size, and content type, check the wording and instructions of the question again.

screens.outro: Now that you've learned the order of judgment, let's summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaways
screens.lead: Summarizes the contents of this class. As you read, answer the opening question: How do we know our limits and how do we respond to them?

paragraphs: The first question was how to know and respond to file format and volume limitations. Limits are checked on four axes: format, number, size, and content type. The unit and number of the limit are different for each product, so rather than memorizing the numbers, check which axis the limit is on.

Large documents are divided into chapters or topics, and a summary file that provides an overall outline and an explanation file with tables and images are provided as supplementary files. Name the files in a way that reveals their content, and prefix each file with a two- or three-line summary to make it easier to search.
Even after sharing, we check whether it has been reflected by asking representative questions. Remember that the limit is not a standard for giving up data, but a standard for splitting data.

Think back to the 300-page report from the first scene. Now, instead of complaining that this file is too big, you can ask where it's stuck along the four axes and choose to split it into chapter files, summaries, and tabular explanations. This approach applies equally to ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini Notebook.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: Just because something falls within the limit doesn't mean it will read well. Refine the material according to format, layout, and volume and check whether it is reflected or not.

glossary.def: The types of files your assistant can read, such as documents, tables, images, and audio.

glossary.term: Number of files and size limits
glossary.def: This is the upper limit of the number and capacity determined by the product and plan.
This is a method of dividing large materials into chapters or topics and organizing only the key points.
This involves supplementing the information in tables and figures with an explanation file that translates it into sentences.

misconceptions.myth: If they are within the limit, they will all be read with the same quality.
misconceptions.fact: The degree of usability varies depending on the format and layout. Tables and images may be processed less smoothly depending on their type.

misconceptions.myth: One large file is safer than many files.
misconceptions.fact: Dividing it into chapters makes it easy to find the piece that fits your question. Putting everything in one file can lead to things you need being buried.

misconceptions.myth: The limit number is the same for all products.
misconceptions.fact: The instructions for GPT, Gemini Notebook, and Claude projects are different, and the units are different: number of files, words, and tokens.

closing.lead: Summarizes what was covered in this class.
points: The limit is the standard for splitting the data.
It is checked on four axes: format, number, size, and content type.
Large documents are divided into chapters, with summaries and table explanations as supplements.
Even after sharing, we check whether it has been reflected by asking representative questions.

checks.q: I uploaded the entire PDF file of the annual report, but only a general answer was given to 'What is the operating profit in the third quarter?' What is the most appropriate action?
options: Divide into chapters with names that reveal the content, and include sentence explanation files for table-based chapters.
Upload the same PDF once again with the same name to increase its weight.
Shorten the question and enter only ‘operating profit’.
Convert the file to an image and upload it to display the table as is.
checks.explain: Dividing large documents into chapters or topics makes it easier to find the pieces that fit your question. For chapters with many tables, it is safe to use auxiliary files that translate key figures into sentences.

wrong.1: Duplicate uploads with the same name may result in mixed content and do not solve the volume issue.
wrong.2: Reducing the number of questions doesn't make it easier to find supporting pieces.
wrong.3: Depending on the type, images may be processed less smoothly, which is disadvantageous in reading tables.
